chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said:
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the first said: 'When death presented itself to my father, he said to me: O my son, indeed the one who takes prayer lightly will not attain our intercession.'
ai.seo_question: Who will not receive the intercession of the Imams according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) conveying a final instruction from his father, Imam al-Hadi (peace be upon him), emphasizing that轻视 (taking lightly) of Salah is a barrier to Ahl al-Bayt's intercession. In Shia scholarship, this underscores that while intercession is a core tenet, it is contingent upon the preservation of the primary pillar of worship, linking spiritual status directly to ritual fidelity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Abu Ismail Al Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘Abu Al-Hassanasws the 1st said: ‘When the death presented itself to myasws fatherasws, heasws said to measws: ‘Weasws will not extend ourasws intercession towards the one who takes Salāt’ lightly.
en.sarwar: 15. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from abu ’Isma‘il al-Sarraj from ibn Muskan from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Abu al-Hassan the first, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When my father was about to pass away he said, “My son, those who consider Salah (prayers) insignificant will not be able to benefit from our intercession.’””
